newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLAMES NAME BRIAN SUTTER HEAD COACH.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLAMES NAME BRIAN SUTTER HEAD COACH.

text.p: Brian Sutter, who has not coached in the National Hockey League since being fired by the Boston Bruins following the 1994-95 season, Thursday was named head coach of the Calgary Flames.
Sutter replaces Pierre Page, who resigned June 18 amid speculation he would fill the coaching vacancy with the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim.
The 40-year-old Sutter compiled a 120-73-23 record in three seasons with the Bruins, but was never able to get past the second round of the playoffs.
He was runner-up for the Adams Award as NHL Coach of the Year in 1992-93 -- his first season in Boston -- after guiding the Bruins to their first 50-win campaign in a decade (51-26-7).
Sutter began his coaching career in 1988-89 with St Louis after spending his entire 12-year NHL playing career with the Blues.
In four years as Blues coach, Sutter posted a 153-124-43 record, winning the Adams Award in 1990-91 after leading St Louis to a 47-22-11 record -- second overall in the league with 105 points.
"What Brian Sutter brings is compatibility and outstanding coaching ability, as proven by his winning record," said Calgary general manager Al Coates.
"He will be a strong motivator and teacher for our young players."
Sutter joins his brother, Darryl, in the NHL coaching fraternity. Darryl Sutter was named San Jose Sharks coach on June 9. Brian and Darryl were two of the six hockey-playing Sutter brothers.
Philadelphia, Anaheim and Buffalo are the remaining NHL teams without a head coach.
